questions.question: What is a partition of a set $S$?
options: A collection of overlapping subsets whose union is empty.
One event with probability one-half
An ordered list of probabilities only
Nonempty disjoint subsets whose union is $S$.
questions.explanation: A partition of $S$ is a collection of nonempty, pairwise-disjoint subsets whose union is all of $S$.
questions.source_support: The definition says a partition is a collection of nonempty subsets whose union is $S$ and whose pairwise intersections are empty.

option_explanations: Overlapping subsets with empty union contradict both partition conditions.
A single event of probability $1/2$ is not a partition of $S$.
A partition is a family of subsets, not an ordered list of probabilities.

questions.question: What does a partition do intuitively?

questions.explanation: A partition splits the sample space into non-overlapping cases that together cover everything.
questions.source_support: The interpretation says a partition splits a space into non-overlapping cases.

questions.question: Which condition makes a partition exhaustive?
options: Every subset is empty
Every pair intersects
The union of the subsets is $S$
The subsets have equal sizes
questions.explanation: A partition is exhaustive when the union of its pieces is all of $S$, so every outcome belongs to at least one piece.
